title: Refuse normalization-ambiguous latent-ceiling corpus scalars
finding: The experiment computed corpus_sha256 from the parsed raw mapping while _nonempty_string silently stripped surrounding whitespace and Corpus.parse lowercased source_revision. Distinct wire payloads could therefore produce the same parsed evidence semantics while retaining different corpus identities, weakening the one-corpus/one-meaning evidence boundary.
primary_claim: The latent-ceiling parser now refuses surrounding whitespace on semantic string fields and requires source_revision to use canonical lowercase 40-hex spelling. Accepted wire payloads are no longer silently normalized into a different semantic Corpus before the corpus hash is retained.
gardener_decision: Tighten the existing scalar parser in place. Do not add a canonicalization service, schema framework, alternate corpus representation, corpus registry, embedding service, vector store, or second evidence identity model.
acceptance: the committed prediction-only corpus remains valid, incomplete, and byte-identical
semantic string fields with surrounding whitespace are refused rather than silently stripped before evidence identity is retained
source_revision with uppercase hexadecimal letters is refused rather than silently lowercased
the existing frozen source revision, frozen denominator, duplicate-key, exact-field, duplicate-row, bucket/status, and evidence-ref refusals remain unchanged
